name: codegent
description: Agentic coding on a free ChatGPT account. ChatGPT reads your GitHub repository, CodeGent applies its changes, checks them and reports back — step by step.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: CodeGent writes files, runs git and can run the verify command you configured.

commands.title: Ask Again Before Committing and Pushing

codegent.autoSubmit.markdownDescription:
Send the prompt in the ChatGPT tab automatically. Turn this off to review the typed prompt and press Enter yourself.

Note: driving a website automatically may not be permitted by that service's terms; check them before enabling.

codegent.autoApply.markdownDescription: Apply ChatGPT's changes without asking. Every step is checkpointed and can be undone. When off, each step is shown for review first.

codegent.autoContinue.markdownDescription: Send each step's result back to ChatGPT automatically so it continues on its own. When off, the run pauses after every step.

codegent.git.commit.markdownDescription: Commit the files each step changed (only those files).

codegent.git.push.markdownDescription: Push after each commit. ChatGPT reads the repository from GitHub, so it only sees a step's changes once they are pushed.

codegent.git.commitPrefix.description: Prefix of the commit messages CodeGent creates.

codegent.maxSteps.description: Stop a run after this many ChatGPT replies.

codegent.maxFailedSteps.description: Stop when this many steps in a row contained changes that could not be applied.

codegent.allowEditingDirtyFiles.markdownDescription: Allow changes to files that have uncommitted modifications. Off by default: ChatGPT cannot see such changes and they would be committed together with CodeGent's.

codegent.chatUrl.markdownDescription: Where new conversations start. Use the URL of a ChatGPT *Project* to start inside it (for example one that already has the GitHub connector enabled). Only chatgpt.com is accepted.

codegent.replyTimeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for ChatGPT to finish a reply.

codegent.browserWaitSeconds.description: How long to wait for the browser extension to connect before giving up on a message.

codegent.conventions.markdownDescription: Standing guidance added to the first message of every run (build tool, code style, things to avoid …).

codegent.verifyCommand.markdownDescription: A command run in the repository after each step that changed files, for example `npm test`. Its result is sent to ChatGPT. Leave empty for none. Can only be set in your user settings.

codegent.verifyTimeoutSeconds.description: Time limit for the verify command.

codegent.diagnosticsWaitSeconds.markdownDescription: How long to let language servers analyse the files a step changed before their errors are collected. Language servers only look at files that are shown in an editor, so CodeGent briefly shows the changed files in a side editor group (without taking focus) and closes them again. Set to 0 to skip this; nothing is opened then.

codegent.advanced.hubPorts.markdownDescription: Local ports on which the hub looks for the browser extension. Leave empty to use the built-in range (47615–47619); the browser extension has to use the same ports.

codegent.advanced.extraBrowserExtensionI.markdownDescription: Ids of additional browser extensions that may connect to the hub, for example your own build of the CodeGent Bridge or a store version. The bundled extension is always allowed; no other browser extension is. Takes effect the next time the hub starts (*CodeGent: Reconnect to the Browser*).
